items.title: Search for Missing Mississauga Paddler Ends in Recovery on a Muskoka Lake
items.summary: According to INsauga, a 31-year-old Mississauga man has died after the canoe he was paddling capsized on Stewart Lake in Georgian Bay Township over the weekend. Ontario Provincial Police say they responded Saturday to a report of a capsized canoe roughly 40 feet from shore, where two people had been on board when it overturned. INsauga reports one occupant was pulled from the water by a passing boater, while the other went under and did not resurface. Police say the missing paddler, the man from Mississauga, was located and confirmed dead on Sunday following a search. The investigation remains open with support from the Office of the Chief Coroner and the Ontario Forensic Pathology Service. INsauga notes the OPP is using the case to remind boaters and paddlers to wear a properly fitted lifejacket or personal flotation device, check weather conditions before heading out and make sure all required safety equipment is on board. Anyone with information about the incident is asked to contact Bracebridge OPP or submit an anonymous tip to Crime Stoppers.

items.title: After Years of Disruption, an LRT Train Is Finally Set to Roll Down Topflight Drive
items.summary: According to INsauga, Ontario Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria announced Friday that a Hazel McCallion Line light rail vehicle is set to begin testing on Topflight Drive in Mississauga next week, following years of construction, delays and road disruptions tied to the project. Sarkaria shared the update in a post on X, saying progress continues on the line, though he did not offer further details on how long the testing would run or how far the train would travel. INsauga reports the significance of this round of testing is that it will happen on the actual LRT corridor itself, rather than being confined to the project's operations, maintenance and storage facility near Highway 407. That facility was the site of an earlier milestone, when Metrolinx said in June that the outdoor rail yard's overhead catenary system had been energized, allowing one of the project's light rail vehicles to operate under its own power for the first time. Metrolinx said at the time that achievement would pave the way for testing vehicles on the line itself, which now appears to be happening. For residents who have lived alongside years of construction along the corridor, next week's test marks one of the first visible signs of trains actually running on Mississauga streets.

items.title: Chase That Began Near Toronto's Esplanade Ends With Three Charged in Fatal Mississauga Shooting
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto police announced Thursday that three people, including 19-year-old Kahiem Bailey-Whitfield of Mississauga, are facing charges tied to the fatal officer-involved shooting that happened earlier this week near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard. Also charged are 23-year-old Naquon Laidley of Toronto and a 17-year-old girl. Police say the case began when officers received a report of a person with a gun near The Esplanade and Lower Jarvis Street in Toronto, and officers from 51 Division identified a suspect vehicle that plainclothes officers then tracked all the way from Toronto into Mississauga. INsauga reports that when officers tried to stop the vehicle near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard, the driver attempted to flee and struck a plainclothes officer in the process. What followed, including the shooting that left a man dead, remains under investigation by Ontario's Special Investigations Unit. Bailey-Whitfield now faces multiple firearms charges, including two counts each of possessing a restricted or prohibited firearm without a licence, occupying a motor vehicle with a firearm, possessing a loaded regulated firearm, and possessing a prohibited weapon without authority.

items.title: Port Credit's Waterfront Turns Into a Rib-Eating Marathon This Weekend, With a Midway Attached
items.summary: According to INsauga, Port Credit Ribfest X 2026 takes over Memorial Park from August 7 to 9, marking the second stop in Mississauga this summer for one of Ontario's biggest rib festivals. Produced by Ontario Festival Group and presented by Gelateria Italiana, the three-day event brings in some of North America's top pitmasters serving smoked ribs, pulled pork, brisket, barbecue chicken, smoked sausage and oversized beef “Dino” ribs. INsauga reports the food lineup extends well beyond barbecue, with vendors including Alabama Lemonade, Billy Bob's Bloomin' Onions, Pineapple Queen, Ontario Corn Roasters and BeaverTails rounding out the offerings alongside poutine, roasted corn and other festival staples. Beyond the food, organizers have built out a full weekend of entertainment and activities, including live music, an artisan marketplace, carnival games, a midway, face painting and a dedicated Kids Zone. The entertainment schedule mixes tribute acts with local bands throughout the weekend, and Friday's lineup features Ida-Maria, Dingo, Pink Leather Jackets and Fiddlestix. For anyone looking to spend a summer weekend on the Port Credit waterfront, the festival offers a packed schedule of food and live entertainment through Sunday.
